judged_text: removeMember and addMembers have no rejection handling anywhere in the chain — the model methods attach no .catch, the inner self.findMembers() reload is neither returned nor caught, and the controller actions discard the returned promises — so a failed membership mutation is invisible. When the PUT/DELETE to /admin/groups/<id>/members.json fails (500, dropped connection), the admin who clicked Add or the remove × sees nothing: no error, no state change, no pending indicator; and even after a successful mutation a failed reload leaves the stale member list with no signal, so the admin cannot tell whether the membership changed.

adjudication.rationale: In `discourse/models/group.js`, both `addMembers` and `removeMember` do `return Discourse.ajax(...).then(function() { self.findMembers(); })` but they neither return the `findMembers()` promise nor attach any rejection handling. That means a failure in the reload request (`findMembers` -> `Discourse.ajax('/groups/<name>/members.json', ...)`) cannot be observed/handled by the original add/remove promise chain. Additionally, in `admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6`, `addMembers` does not return the model promise at all (`this.get("model").addMembers(...)`), and `removeMember` triggers `self.get("model").removeMember(member);` inside the bootbox callback without returning/catching it, so the action layer also provides no way to surface failures. The diff shows no other UI error/pending-state handling around these calls, making silent failures and stale member lists a real risk introduced by this change.
